label: Start construction
summary: A command of the game's interface that, going by its name, starts the construction of a great project.
details: It returns a command, and the game's script files do not use it anywhere. The game documents nothing more.

label: Contribution itself
summary: Hands the great project contribution itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types, it is a plumbing function. The game documents nothing more.

label: Contributor
summary: The one who makes this contribution to the great project.
details: Vanilla uses it in the great project window as the data of a sub-element, and checks whether it is valid to decide what to show. Going by its name, that is the contributing character; the game does not state the type.

label: Contribution name
summary: The name of a contribution to a great project, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in condition texts such as "[contribution] is essential to start working on [project]" and its negative form.

label: Contribution type
summary: The kind of contribution a great project contribution is.
details: Vanilla reads its name in texts about funding: "Can fund [type]", "You can fund ..." and "[character] can fund ...". The game does not register its return type.

label: Is funded
summary: Whether this contribution to the great project has been paid for.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it in the great project windows inside a condition that decides whether an element is shown, together with a check that the project's owner is the player.

label: As script scope
summary: Turns the contribution into a script scope, so script values can be read from it.
details: The game documents it as a promote function returning a scope. Vanilla uses MakeScope on other types, for example on the player to read a script value in a building tooltip.

label: Contribution itself
summary: The contribution itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument to other functions. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Item itself
summary: Hands the great project item itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Cancel project
summary: A command of the interface that, going by its name, cancels the great project this item stands for.
details: It returns nothing, and the game's script files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Great project
summary: The great project this item belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it in the decisions window to set the data of an element to that project.

label: Item description
summary: The description text of the great project item.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game's script files do not use it.

label: Item name
summary: The name of the great project item, as text.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses a call of this name on an available great project item in the decisions window as the text of a label.

label: Project type
summary: The great project type of this item.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses calls of this name in the decisions window and the plan window to set the data of an element to the project type, and to read its player name.

label: Item itself
summary: The great project item itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Map icon itself
summary: Hands the great project map icon itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Great project
summary: The great project shown by this map icon.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer to set the data of an element to that project.

label: Project tag
summary: A short text tag that identifies one great project among the ones on the map icon.
details: Vanilla gives it a great project (`GreatProject.Self`) and stores the result in an interface variable named for the expanded contribution list. It then compares that variable to decide which project's contributions are shown. Going by that use, the tag only tells projects apart.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The great project to make a tag for.

label: Projects on the icon
summary: The list of great projects this map icon stands for.
details: One map icon can cover several projects in the same province. Vanilla counts the list for a "+N" label and skips the first entry when listing the extra ones.

label: Province
summary: The province the map icon sits in.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer to set the data of an element to that province.

label: Icon tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the great project map icon.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game's script files do not use this exact form; other types have a function of the same name that gives their tooltip.

label: Has several projects
summary: Whether the map icon stands for more than one great project.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer, together with a check that the province's list is not already expanded, to decide whether an element is shown.

label: Is project hovered
summary: Whether the given great project is the one the mouse pointer is over on the map icon.
details: Going by its name. The game's script files do not use it. It pairs with the functions that set and reset the hovered project.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The great project to check.

label: Clear hovered project
summary: A command of the interface that, going by its name, forgets which great project is hovered.
details: It returns nothing, and the game's script files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Map icon itself
summary: The great project map icon itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Set hovered project
summary: A command of the interface that, going by its name, marks the given great project as the hovered one.
details: It returns nothing, and the game's script files do not use it. It pairs with the check for a hovered project.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The great project to mark as hovered.

label: Project type itself
summary: Hands the great project type itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Custom text
summary: Runs one of the game's named custom texts on the great project type and returns the result.
details: Going by its name and how Custom is used on other types: vanilla writes the name of a custom localization in quotes, for example on a character. The game's script files do not use it on this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom localization to run.

label: Cannot plan reason
summary: The text that says why a great project of this type cannot be planned in the given province by the given planner.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the plan window, giving a province and the planning character (`Province.Self`, `PlanGreatProjectWindow.GetPlanner.Self`).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province the project would be planned in.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who would plan it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Contribution deadline percent
summary: A fixed-point number that, going by its name, is the deadline for contributions as a percentage.
details: The game's script files do not use it, and it does not say what the percentage is of. The game documents nothing more.

label: Contribution descriptions
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes the contributions of this project type.
details: It takes one argument whose meaning is not documented, and the game's script files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented by the game.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the great project type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the plan window as a text, and in the tooltip that shows when you hover a project choice, under the project's name.

label: Item description tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that describes a great project item of this type for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the decisions window (with the planner character of the item) and in the intrigue window (with the puppet character).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the tooltip is written for.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the planner or puppet `.Self`

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the great project type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the decisions window as the texture of an image.

label: Illustration
summary: The illustration picture of the great project type, chosen for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it in the decisions window (with the planner character) and the intrigue window (with the puppet) as an image texture.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the illustration is chosen for.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the planner or puppet `.Self`

label: Index
summary: The number of the great project type in the game's list of types.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. The game's script files do not use this exact form.

label: Key
summary: The script key of the great project type, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game's script files do not use this exact form; other types' GetKey show their key, for example in debug texts.

label: Mandatory contributions cost
summary: Text that, going by its name, shows what the required contributions of this project type cost in the given province.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province (`Province.Self`).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province the project is planned in.

label: Name
summary: The name of the great project type, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in a map mode text that says the project cannot be planned in the given title. The text carries a tooltip; the NoTooltip form gives the plain name.

label: Name for character
summary: The name of the great project type as it reads for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it in the intrigue window, giving the puppet character, as a text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the name is written for.

label: Name for character, plain
summary: The name of the great project type for the given character, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name, it is the form of the character-specific name without the hover tooltip. The game's script files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the name is written for.

label: Name for player
summary: The name of the great project type as it reads for the player.
details: Vanilla uses it in the plan window as a text.

label: Name for player, plain
summary: The name of the great project type for the player, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name, it is the form of the player name without the hover tooltip. The game's script files do not use it.

label: Name, plain
summary: The name of the great project type, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of a project choice, in bold above the description.

label: Possessive name, plain
summary: The great project type's name in its possessive form, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla's one use puts it after the name of a character's house, in the text for a great project's possessive name.

label: Plan cost
summary: Text that, going by its name, shows what it costs to plan this project type in the given province, for the given planner.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province and the planning character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province the project would be planned in.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who would plan it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Plan requirements
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes what is required to plan this project type.
details: It takes one argument whose meaning is not documented, and the game's script files do not use it. The in-province form is used in the plan window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented by the game.

label: Plan requirements in province
summary: Text that, going by its name, lists what is required to plan this project type in the given province, for the given planner.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province and the planning character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province the project would be planned in.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who would plan it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Completed effects text
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes what happens when a project of this type is completed.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province and the planning character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province of the project.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who plans it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Failed effects text
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes what happens when a project of this type fails.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province and the planning character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province of the project.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who plans it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Owner description
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes the owner of a project of this type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province and the planning character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province of the project.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who plans it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Started effects text
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes what happens when a project of this type is started.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the plan window, giving the province and the planning character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province of the project.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who plans it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Is enabled by puppet
summary: Whether the project type is available through a puppet, going by its name.
details: The game's script files do not use it on this type. Vanilla uses a function of the same name on decisions to show elements, so the name probably means the same here, but that is a hint only.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the great project type is valid, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by the same-named function on other types: vanilla uses IsValid to check a thing before using it. The game's script files do not use it on this type.

label: Localize
summary: Looks up the localized text for the given key.
details: Going by its name. The game's script files do not use it on this type; other uses of Localize in vanilla texts give it a text key and return the translated text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The localization key to look up.
fields.values: a quoted key, or a text built with Concatenate

label: Needs location choice
summary: Whether the player has to pick a location on the map for a project of this type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the plan window to show or hide parts, for example together with a check whether the picked province satisfies the requirements.

label: Meets requirements
summary: Whether the given province and planner meet the requirements to plan a project of this type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the plan window to show or hide elements, for the selected province and for the province under the mouse.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province the project would be planned in.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character who would plan it.
fields.values: a character, in vanilla the window's planner `.Self`

label: Project type itself
summary: The great project type itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla passes it to functions that take a project type, for example to open the plan window for it and to start planning a project in a province.

label: Show owner portrait
summary: Whether the owner's portrait should be shown for projects of this type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla reaches it through a project's type (`GreatProject.GetType`) in the decisions and great project windows, together with a check that the character is valid and not the local player.

label: Mandatory contributions
summary: The list of required contributions of the great project shown in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a list element in the great project window, and checks whether it is empty to show a note instead.

label: Optional contributions
summary: The list of optional contributions of the great project shown in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a list element, and checks whether it has items or is empty to decide what to show.

label: Window itself
summary: Hands the great project window itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can afford selected
summary: Whether the given character can pay for the contributions currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it the player. It is used, together with a check that something is selected, to enable an element, and in a tooltip that shows when the answer is no.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would pay.

label: Can cancel project
summary: Whether the given character can cancel the great project shown in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it the player, and shows an element when this is true and no contributions are selected.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who wants to cancel.

label: Can contribute
summary: Whether the given character can contribute to the great project shown in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it the player and uses it as the condition for showing an element.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who wants to contribute.

label: Can show contributor list
summary: Whether the window can show the list of potential contributors.
details: Vanilla uses it in a condition together with a check that the project's owner is the player, to decide whether an element of a contribution is shown.

label: Can start with selection
summary: Whether the project can be started with the contributions currently selected.
details: Vanilla uses it to choose between two button texts: one for starting the project with the selection and one for only funding the contributions.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the great project window.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click handler in the great project window.

label: Fund contributions
summary: Pays for the selected contributions with the given character.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it with the player from a click handler in the great project window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who pays.

label: Cannot afford text
summary: The text that explains why the given character cannot afford the selected contributions.
details: Vanilla gives it the player and shows the text as a tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would pay.

label: Great project
summary: The great project the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it in the great project window to set the data of an element to that project.

label: Selected cost
summary: Text that, going by its name, shows what the selected contributions cost the given character.
details: Vanilla gives it the player and shows the result as a text in the window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would pay.

label: Selected effects text
summary: Text that, going by its name, describes the effects of the selected contributions.
details: The game's script files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has selection
summary: Whether any contribution is currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show an element, to enable one together with the affordability check, and to hide one while something is selected.

label: Window itself
summary: The great project window itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Ask to cancel project
summary: Shows a confirmation for cancelling the great project, going by its name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click handler in the great project window.

label: Show potential contributors
summary: Shows the list of potential contributors for the given contribution.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it with the clicked contribution row (`ContributionItem.Self`) in the great project window and the plan window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The contribution to list contributors for.

label: Group itself
summary: Hands the group itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. Vanilla only shows Group in the achievements screen. The game documents nothing more.

label: Visible achievements
summary: The list of achievements of the group that are visible.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a list element in the achievements types GUI file.

label: Unlocked visible count
summary: The number of visible achievements of the group that are unlocked, going by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. The game's script files do not use it.

label: Group name
summary: The name of the group, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game's script files do not use this exact form; the same-named function is common on other types.

label: Visible count
summary: The number of visible achievements in the group, going by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. The game's script files do not use it.

label: Is collapsed
summary: Whether the group is folded closed in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it in the achievements screen to pick the frame of an image and to hide the group's content when it is collapsed.

label: Group itself
summary: The group itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Fold or unfold
summary: Folds the group closed if it is open, and open if it is closed.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from click handlers in the achievements GUI file.

label: Coordinator itself
summary: Hands the AI war coordinator itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Cached enemy power
summary: The enemy side's power value that the AI war coordinator has stored, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window next to the allied value, as "Cached Power (Allied/Enemy)".

label: Cached enemy strength
summary: The enemy side's strength value that the AI war coordinator has stored, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window next to the allied value, as "Cached Strength (Allied/Enemy)".

label: Cached allied power
summary: The allied side's power value that the AI war coordinator has stored, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window before the enemy value, as "Cached Power (Allied/Enemy)".

label: Cached allied strength
summary: The allied side's strength value that the AI war coordinator has stored, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window before the enemy value, as "Cached Strength (Allied/Enemy)".

label: Current power
summary: The current power value of the AI war coordinator, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window before the maximum, as "Power (Current/Max)".

label: Current strength
summary: The current strength value of the AI war coordinator, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window before the maximum, as "Strength (Current/Max)".

label: Max power
summary: The maximum power value of the AI war coordinator, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window after the current value, as "Power (Current/Max)".

label: Max strength
summary: The maximum strength value of the AI war coordinator, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug window after the current value, as "Strength (Current/Max)".

label: War stance
summary: The AI's current stance in the war, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in bold in a debug window as "AI War Stance". The window is a developer tool, not part of the normal game screens.

label: Is active
summary: Whether the AI war coordinator is turned on.
details: Vanilla uses it in the debug window to choose the toggle button's label: "Disable" when active, "Enable" when not.

label: Is desperate
summary: Whether the AI war coordinator counts the war as desperate.
details: Vanilla uses it in the debug window to show "Is Desperate" or "Is NOT Desperate". The game does not say what makes the AI desperate.

label: Is shown
summary: Whether the AI war coordinator's debug window content is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it to choose the button label "Hide" or "Show" and to show or hide the panel.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the AI war coordinator exists.
details: Vanilla uses it as the condition for showing the debug window's content.

label: Coordinator itself
summary: The AI war coordinator itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Show units list
summary: Opens the list of units, going by its name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the debug window.

label: Switch on or off
summary: Turns the AI war coordinator on if it is off, and off if it is on.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click handler in the debug window, next to a label that switches between "Disable" and "Enable" with the active state.

label: Show or hide
summary: Shows the AI war coordinator's panel if it is hidden, and hides it if it is shown.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a click handler in the debug window, next to a label that switches between "Hide" and "Show" with the shown state.

label: Item itself
summary: Hands the important action item itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Important action
summary: The important action this item stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD notification templates to set the data of an element to that action.

label: Item itself
summary: The important action item itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Action item itself
summary: Hands the action item itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Dismiss
summary: Dismisses the notification item, going by its name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it on a right click on the notification in the HUD.

label: Action item
summary: An action item, going by its name.
details: The game's script files do not use it, and it does not say which item it gives back. The game documents nothing more.

label: Action type
summary: The type of action the item stands for.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses the same-named call on important action items in the HUD templates, then checks whether the type is dangerous. Not used on this type itself.

label: Combined group label
summary: The label text of a group of combined notifications.
details: Vanilla uses it in a localization text for the combined notification label, which simply shows this value.

label: Combined group name
summary: The name of a group of combined notifications, as text, going by its name.
details: The game's script files do not use it.

label: Combined tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a group of combined notifications.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip of the notification in the HUD templates.

label: First visible item
summary: The first notification item in the list that is visible.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates to set the data of an element to that item.

label: Important action items
summary: The list of important action items inside this notification.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a list element in the HUD templates.

label: Visible item count
summary: How many items of the notification are visible, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the HUD templates.

label: Has dangerous action
summary: Whether any action in the notification is marked as dangerous.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates to pick between two looks of a notification: one for dangerous and one for ordinary ones, both only when the item is not unimportant.

label: Has several actions
summary: Whether the notification combines more than one action.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates, with the visibility check, to choose between the single and the combined look.

label: Is expanded
summary: Whether the notification is unfolded to show its items.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates to show an element and to pick the frame of an image.

label: Is read
summary: Whether the notification has been marked as read.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates, negated, to show an element only while the notification is still unread.

label: Is unimportant
summary: Whether the notification is marked as unimportant.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates, negated, so that only important notifications get the dangerous or ordinary highlight.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the notification is currently visible.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD templates together with the several-actions check, to choose between the single and the combined look.

label: Mark as read
summary: Marks the notification as read.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it when the mouse pointer enters the notification.

label: Click action
summary: Does what a click on the notification does.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the click handler of the notification in the HUD templates. The game does not say what the click does.

label: Action item itself
summary: The action item itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types: vanilla passes the object itself as an argument. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Curve editor itself
summary: Hands the animation curve editor itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: This belongs to the game's built-in editor tools, not to normal screens. Going by its name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Graph line
summary: The curve lines drawn in the engine's GUI animation curve editor.
details: Its one use fills the curve editor's graph area; each line has its own color, the points it is drawn through and its control points. The game does not register its return type.

label: Timeline editor open
summary: Going by its name and its use, whether the GUI animation (timeline) editor is open.
details: In the engine's curve editor it marks the "Timeline Editor" button as pressed; that button opens the GUI animation editor. The game documents nothing more.

label: Curve editor itself
summary: The animation curve editor itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types. This is one of the game's built-in editor tools. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Control point itself
summary: Hands the curve editor control point itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: This belongs to the game's built-in editor tools. Going by its name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Control point position
summary: Where a control point sits in the curve editor's graph, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: The engine's curve editor places the control point's marker there.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether a control point in the curve editor is selected.
details: The engine's curve editor shows the marker's selected picture when this is true and the mouse is not over it. Vanilla passes the animation editor's shared state as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The animation editor's shared state, where the selection is kept.

label: Is under mouse
summary: Whether the mouse pointer is over a control point in the curve editor.
details: The engine's curve editor then shows the marker's hover picture, before checking whether it is selected.

label: Control point itself
summary: The curve editor control point itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types. This is one of the game's built-in editor tools. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Curve line itself
summary: Hands the curve editor line itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: This belongs to the game's built-in editor tools. Going by its name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Line color
summary: The color a curve line is drawn in, as four numbers (red, green, blue and transparency).
details: Its one use colors the line in the engine's curve editor graph.

label: Control point
summary: The control points of a curve line in the curve editor.
details: Its one use draws a marker for each one on the line in the engine's curve editor. The game does not register its return type.

label: Line points
summary: The points a curve line is drawn through in the curve editor.
details: Its one use gives the line its points in the engine's curve editor graph. The game does not register its return type.

label: Curve line itself
summary: The curve editor line itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types. This is one of the game's built-in editor tools. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Viewport itself
summary: Hands the curve editor viewport itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: This belongs to the game's built-in editor tools. Going by its name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Needle position
summary: The position of the time needle in the curve editor viewport, as a pair of numbers, going by its name.
details: It takes three arguments whose meaning is not documented. The return type is a 2D vector. The game's script files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented by the game.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Not documented by the game.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: Not documented by the game.

label: Viewport itself
summary: The curve editor viewport itself, to be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types. This is one of the game's built-in editor tools. The game documents nothing more here.

label: Animation set
summary: The animation sets shown in the engine's GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use fills the "Animation Sets:" list; each entry shows its name and can be selected. The game does not register its return type.

label: Animation
summary: The animations of the animation set selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use fills the "Animations:" list, described as the animations of the currently selected animation set. The game does not register its return type.

label: Available track
summary: The tracks offered in the GUI animation editor's dialog for adding a track.
details: Its one use fills that dialog: each entry shows its name and description and adds the track when clicked, unless it is excluded. The game does not register its return type.

label: Animation editor itself
summary: Hands the animation editor itself to the interface, in a form that can be passed on.
details: This belongs to the game's built-in editor tools. Going by its name and by how the same-named function is used on other interface types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Universal tracks
summary: The list of universal animation tracks in the animation editor, going by its name.
details: The game's script files do not use it. It is part of the game's built-in editor tools.

label: Add keyframes now
summary: Adds a keyframe at the current time to every visible track of the GUI animation editor.
details: Its button's tooltip says so, and adds that a double-click on a track makes a keyframe on that track alone. It returns nothing.

label: Can change set parent
summary: Whether the GUI animation editor can change which animation set the selected set inherits from.
details: It turns on the button that does this.

label: Can create animation
summary: Whether a new animation can be created in the selected animation set of the GUI animation editor.
details: It turns on the button for a new animation.
